question.problem:
$\,$ $0\le 2$ and $4.3$ is not irrational

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(0\le 2\text{ and }4.3\text{ is not irrational}) & ≡¬((0\le 2)∧(4.3\text{ is not irrational})) \\  & ≡¬(0\le 2)∨¬(4.3\text{ is not irrational}) \\  & ≡(0>2)∨(4.3\text{ is irrational}) \\  & ≡(0>2)\text{ or }4.3\text{ is irrational}.\end{aligned}
$$
